verdicts.evidence: The condition x_1 | (x_1-1)(x_2-1) implies x_1 | x_2-1. For x_1 = 8p^k and x_2 = 3^{x_1/2}, this requires 3^{4p^k} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^k}, which implies the order of 3 modulo p must divide 4. This only happens for p=2 and p=5. Candidate A (p \neq 3) includes many other primes (e.g., p=7) that do not satisfy this condition.

verdicts.label: B
verdicts.evidence: The condition x_1 | x_2-1 is necessary and sufficient for the product x_1...x_n to divide (x_1-1)...(x_{n+1}-1) for all n. For x_1 = 8p^k and x_2 = 3^{x_1/2}, this condition holds if and only if the order of 3 modulo p divides 4, which occurs only for p=2 and p=5. This was confirmed for small k and n.
